SMTO-JOB-0010 — The task tried to wait for something it hasn't seen

GUID: c48a2eaa-17eb-4300-8585-9965bbdb1779
Slug: wait-event-scope-invalid
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • The agent asked to pause until a particular event happened, but that event doesn't appear in anything this task has produced. The wait wasn't set, so the task isn't paused.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply in the conversation with what the task should wait for, such as a job it started finishing, or ask it to wait a set time, for example 15 minutes. A timed wait, or a wait on something this task started, can be set up without this check failing.
  2. If the event belongs to a different conversation, start or check that work in this conversation instead of pointing at the other one. A task can only wait on events from its own results, not from unrelated conversations.
  3. Don't type or paste an event reference for the agent; let it use one it received from its own steps. SMTO refuses references it can't find in this task's results, so a copied or guessed one fails again.

What success looks like

  • The task shows it is waiting, and it continues when the event happens or the time is up.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't point the task at an event from an unrelated conversation to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An event wait named an event_id that does not appear in any result recorded by this run, so wait_for_event rejected it as unknown or out of scope.

What this means

  • An event wait cannot find the requested event among events observed in the current authorized scope. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • An event wait cannot find the requested event among events observed in the current authorized scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current owned event references instead of guessing IDs from another task.

How to fix it

  • wait_for_event only accepts an event_id found in this run's stored result data (the run's recorded results). Use an ID returned by a tool result in the same run, or use a kind=time wait with wake_at or delay_seconds; do not guess IDs or reuse one from another conversation.
  • Select an event ID returned by supported observation in this scope. Do not guess IDs or wait on an unrelated conversation’s event.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The wait uses an exact event returned by supported observation in this scope.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
